definition.name: Pairing phase D - native teardown and reachable cancellation

nodes.label: R5 native terminal and cancellation owner
nodes.task_summary: Fix iOS native TCP termination, cancellation and owned-worker teardown
nodes.prompt: TASK: Implement the iOS native lifecycle owner required by R5/R6. DELIVERABLE: scoped native code and tests plus .omo/pairing-20260910/reports/d-native.md. SCOPE: ios-shell/src/state.rs, commands.rs, lib.rs registration if needed, native tests and native test-only manifest dependencies. Read core session APIs but do not change them without reporting the exact needed contract to the coordinator. Do not touch UI or desktop. Consume RuntimeEvents, propagate generation-bound terminal reason, stop/join runtime and workers, release input, clean up audio failures, and cancel in-progress native connection without waiting behind its lifecycle lock. Keep serialized ownership transfer. VERIFY: failing-first production-owner tests, including real authenticated loopback TCP remote close with UDP silent, stale terminal event ignored, canceled connect cannot install resources, and worker completion signals; run cargo test --manifest-path clients/rust/Cargo.toml -p erd-ios on Omarchy plus exact newly named tests and diagnostics. STOP WHEN: actual RED/GREEN evidence and complete scoped code/report delivered with no owned test resources remaining. Read .omo/pairing-20260910/phase-d-handoff.md, contracts.md, and docs/remote-connection-pairing-review-plan-20260910.md before edits. All handoff constraints bind. Append exact new regression names and RED commands to the existing append-only notepad before RED; capture lifecycle-* evidence. Rust check/test/build ONLY through SSH indo@100.91.254.71 at /home/indo/projects/erd-pairing-20260910 with FFmpeg7 environment; sync only owned changed files. No commits, model-setting changes, emulators, installs/deploys, production host changes or edits outside your scope. Preserve all C identity behavior and unrelated changes. Use event-driven deterministic tests and monitors. Lead owns physical-device QA and final review; distinguish missing physical evidence from passed fixtures.
